title: Built a Resident Evil-style outbreak scene in Blender using only AI agent
author: hi3d_official
selftext:
![img](hruhs4wxvdwh1 "1 · Final render")

![img](5qker910wdwh1 "2 · Model layout")

![img](u1vjk9j1wdwh1 "3 · Blender blockout")

The new Resident Evil movie got me thinking about that first night of an outbreak. Empty streets, ambulance lights bleeding through fog, and someone standing in the middle of the road who probably shouldn't be there.

Had this scene stuck in my head, so I spent the weekend trying to recreate that feeling in Blender. One rule: no manual modeling or lighting. Everything had to go through an AI agent.

I started by having the agent generate a concept image to nail down the atmosphere and composition. Then I used Hi3D to generate the main assets: a character, ambulance, wheelchair, zombies, etc. The agent imported everything into Blender, blocked out the street, and pulled in some free assets from Fab to fill out the environment.

The first result was... way too clean. Looked more like a Halloween-themed street than the end of the world lol.

So I kept giving feedback in plain English:

"Too even. I want corners I can't see into."

"Tilt the camera about 5 degrees. Something feels too comfortable."

"The ground looks waxed. Give me ugly wet asphalt and puddles."

The agent also generated detailed textures for the road, walls, and vehicles. For the distant buildings, I went with AI-generated matte painting matched to the Blender camera instead of modeling an entire city.

![img](3z1hkn36wdwh1 "4 · Asset pass. The barely-visible background figures do most of the horror work — cheap trick, works every time.")



![img](612a8sx7wdwh1 "5 · A normal evening of directing: 'deeper fog, darker corners, tilt it, make the floor uglier.' It re-lights between every message.")

![img](jp37as3awdwh1 "6 · Same street, six conversations apart. Lookdev is just arguing with a very patient machine.")

So basically: **concept art → Hi3D assets → Blender blockout → Fab assets → textures → lighting → matte painting → final render.**

Honestly, the hardest part wasn't the tech. It was figuring out how to explain *why* something felt wrong instead of just saying "make it better."

Still plenty I'd improve, but pretty happy with this little experiment. Process shots are in the gallery, including that ridiculous wall of light rigs.
